newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica Volkswagen plant shut amid protests.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica Volkswagen plant shut amid protests.

text.p: About 4,500 workers at German car maker Volkswagen's Uitenhage plant in South Africa's Eastern Cape province downed tools on Tuesday in protest at the company's cost-cutting measures, a spokesman said.

Volkswagen's Raymond Hartle said the plant had come to a standstill early on Tuesday after workers belonging to the National Union of Metalworkers of South Africa (NUMSA) refused to return to work following a mass meeting.
The Uitenhage plant has a daily output of around 320 vehicles worth about 30 million rand, Hartle said.
"Effectively what has happened is that the production area has been shut, so we are looking at about 4,500 being affected. Non-production areas are still operating," he told Reuters.

He said union leaders attributed their members' action to unhappiness with some of the company's cost-cutting proposals such as the requirement that workers who lease the firm's cars contribute to insurance costs.
Hartle said the company had also announced stricter enforcement of the company's policy on absenteeism during talks with the union leaders on Monday.
The strikers had also complained about erratic production at the plant's paint shop, Hartle added.

"The company has introduced more stringent quality control measures, particularly in the paint shop, aimed at improving the quality of vehicles delivered to customers. In the early implementation of these measures, some disruption downstream has been experienced," he said in a statement.

Hartle said the strike came amid talks by Volkswagen and the union to try find an amicable way of implementing the cost-cutting proposals, adding that further negotiations between the two parties were under way on Tuesday to resolve the impasse.
Union leaders were unavailable for comment.
